newsitem.title: USA: America Online to announce pricing moves.
newsitem.headline: America Online to announce pricing moves.

text.p: America Online Inc, the world's largest online service, is expected to announce much-anticipated pricing changes on Tuesday, as well as new technologies and directions for the future, analysts said.
America Online, based in Dulles, Va., is expected to unveil a new pricing structure, with possibly three new levels of pricing, including a $19.95 a month levy for unlimited access.
It would be a response to the new pricing of Microsoft Corp, which relaunched the Microsoft Network a few weeks ago.
"They will do some pricing changes," said Abhishek Gami, an analyst with Nesbitt Burns Securities.
The company is holding a conference call with Wall Street analysts at 800 EST on Tuesday morning and a press conference later that day in New York.
Officials at America Online could not be immediately reached for comment.

Analysts said the online service, which has been undergoing many changes and pressures in recent months as its subscriber growth has slowed, will also discuss some other new pricing points, new technologies and the next version of AOL, code-named Casablanca, targeted for first quarter 1997.
"I think there will be lot of introductions tomorrow," said Gary Arlen, president of Arlen Communications, in Bethesda, Md.

AOL is also expoected to demonstrate new technologies, such as streaming audio technology, for faster audio, and AOL Phone, similar to the current Internet phone technology, where subscribers in other cities or in countries like Britain, France, Germany, and Japan, can talk to each other over a speaker phone on the PC, while logged onto AOL, for free.
"They will focus on their new technologies," Gami said.
